title: tier-2 shipped code: CDN index footer parse against the client's FUN_1424d9af0
notes: SHIPPED-CODE tier-2 unit. The candidate is crates/ow-casc/src/container.rs, built by cargo and called by crates/ow-casc/src/bin/verify_probe.rs through the cdn_index_footer_parse entry. The ledger binds the verdict to container.rs + the probe source + the git revision.

Oracle is FUN_1424d9af0 at exe 0x1424d9af0. Signature: (void *buffer, uint32 buffer_len, uint32 file_len, uint8 out[0x30]). The client reads the footer at buffer + buffer_len - 20; the probe passes the footer at the end of a 64-byte arena buffer and the same len field, so the address is the same. The function writes only AL: on success it does `XOR AL,AL` after leaving the total length in EAX, so RAX is `file_len & ~0xff`, not 0; on a reject AL=8 and RAX's upper bits hold whatever the last compare left. Callers test AL only, so the unit declares `void` and compares the memory channel.

Output layout, verified against the function bytes: out[0..0x14] is the footer copy; out[0x14]=pageSize=footer[3]<<10; out[0x18]=entrySize=footer[4]+footer[5]+footer[6]; out[0x1c]=pageSize/entrySize; out[0x20]=(elementCount-1+entriesPerPage)/entriesPerPage; out[0x24]=pageCount*keyBytes; out[0x28]=pageCount*checksumSize. All derived fields are host-order dwords and all arithmetic is 32-bit wrapping.

The memory channel carries every accept/reject that is caller-visible: a bad footer hash leaves out[0xc..0x14] zeroed; a version, checksum-size, zero-page, zero-entry or zero-entries-per-page reject leaves all derived fields untouched at the fixture's 0xA5 fill; an accepted geometry writes the six dwords. Both buffers are compared, so an unintended input write is caught too.

The one status the memory channel cannot see is the final length gate: the client writes the same six dwords and then returns 8 when file_len is one byte off. The unit pins both edges so coverage reaches the branch, and container.rs's own tests plus the four real files prove the length formula; the status itself is the declared gap.

Real cases: the four install footers (archive-group 0100000406041008d847970055a616cfef3af752 at 260,173,908 B; patch group 01000004050410081e591d00e8d1710213451589 at 48,616,028 B; file-index 0100000400041008d66e0000f82dc775fc579b5b at 576,828 B; patch file index 01000004000410084a110000909b13e32eae4b30 at 90,668 B). The fixture pins them at prefix 0 and 44, so the footer-at-the-end read is exercised at two addresses.

The sweep also pins version 0/1/2/3/0xff, checksum 0/1/16/17/0xff, page sizes 0/1/2/255 KiB, zero entry components and every key/size/offset zero combination, and element counts 0/1/156/157/158/314/315/0xffffffff (the 157-entry boundary of the real archive group). A wrong header hash is pinned with an otherwise valid length so the hash branch is reached first.

Not tested: a buffer_len below 20. The client computes buffer + len - 20 and would read before the buffer, so no representable arena input can make that a defined call; the probe rejects it before calling the port. The divide-by-zero edge (page size smaller than the entry size) is likewise unreachable through the footer bytes: the largest entry sum is 765 and the smallest nonzero page is 1024, so entriesPerPage is never zero. The port keeps a guard for it, but the unit cannot produce the input.

allowedImageReads: 0x7ff7c87e5f40-0x7ff7c87e5f47 is the /GS security cookie at exe 0x143ac5f40; 0x7ff7c87e5f98-0x7ff7c87e5faf is the CRT memcpy feature-flag block at exe 0x143ac5f98; 0x7ff7c83395c0-0x7ff7c83395df is a compiler dispatch table at exe 0x1436195c0; 0x7ff7c818b2b0-0x7ff7c818b2ff is the error-format string block (`\x%02x`, `%03o`, hex digits, `%.*g`) at exe 0x14346b2b0. They are fixed image data read by the MD5 helper, the stack check and the reject logger, not game state.

knownEquivalentMutants.rationale: Line 1162 is the final `if expected != total_len` gate. Flipping it to `==` changes only the value the client leaves in AL; both branches write the same six geometry dwords before the compare, and the unit's void/memory channel cannot see AL. The mutant is therefore observationally equivalent in every channel this unit compares, not in the client's caller-visible status. What would kill it: a return-mask channel for AL, which the runner does not have. container.rs's own tests assert the length reject directly.

acknowledgedGaps.why: On a length mismatch the client writes the same six geometry dwords as an accept and only AL differs (8 vs 0), so the void/memory channel cannot distinguish the two. The length formula itself is proven by the four real index files and by container.rs's synthetic tests; the harness would need a return-mask channel that the runner does not have. RAX cannot substitute: on success the client leaves `file_len & ~0xff` in EAX, and on a reject its upper bits are whatever the last compare left, neither of which a caller uses.

acknowledgedGaps.what: A buffer shorter than the 20-byte footer
acknowledgedGaps.why: The client subtracts 20 from the length without a guard and reads before the buffer; the oracle cannot represent the resulting wild read, and a fault is not a behaviour. Every defined call has buffer_len >= 20, which the fixture covers.
